# Aunt Jamesina

## Overview

- **Gender:** female  <sub>[v3 c16 P52](../source/v03-c16.md#nw-v03-c16-p0052)</sub>
- **Role:** Housekeeper / housemother  <sub>[v3 c9 P13](../source/v03-c09.md#nw-v03-c09-p0013), [v3 c35 P5](../source/v03-c35.md#nw-v03-c35-p0005), [v3 c37 P12](../source/v03-c37.md#nw-v03-c37-p0012)</sub>
- **Titles:** queen of housemothers  <sub>[v3 c35 P5](../source/v03-c35.md#nw-v03-c35-p0005)</sub>
- **Nicknames:** Aunt Jimsie  <sub>[v3 c9 P13](../source/v03-c09.md#nw-v03-c09-p0013)</sub>; Aunty J.  <sub>[v3 c24 P5](../source/v03-c24.md#nw-v03-c24-p0005)</sub>

## Appearance

Aunt Jamesina is a tiny old woman with a softly-triangular face, pink cheeks, and snow-white hair worn in quaint little puffs over her ears. She has large, soft blue eyes filled with youthful light and hope. She dresses in an old-fashioned style.

_Sources: [v3 c16 P52](../source/v03-c16.md#nw-v03-c16-p0052), [v3 c16 P53](../source/v03-c16.md#nw-v03-c16-p0053)_

## Personality

She is sweet, cheerful, mirthful, and holds an old-fashioned worldview while remaining indulgence-minded and easygoing toward the youth under her care. Though she scolds lightly and maintains a proper respect for the clergy, she harbors a playful streak, openly admitting to having made fun of her own suitors in her youth.

_Sources: [v3 c9 P13](../source/v03-c09.md#nw-v03-c09-p0013), [v3 c16 P53](../source/v03-c16.md#nw-v03-c16-p0053), [v3 c18 P2](../source/v03-c18.md#nw-v03-c18-p0002), [v3 c19 P4](../source/v03-c19.md#nw-v03-c19-p0004), [v3 c35 P21](../source/v03-c35.md#nw-v03-c35-p0021), [v3 c37 P42](../source/v03-c37.md#nw-v03-c37-p0042)_

## Goals

- to get a yellow silk dress in heaven  <sub>[v3 c19 P6](../source/v03-c19.md#nw-v03-c19-p0006)</sub>

## History

Aunt Jamesina was named after her father James, who drowned at sea a month prior to her birth. After her only daughter, Elizabeth, married and moved to India as a foreign missionary, Aunt Jamesina was left alone in a large house. She agreed to move to Kingsport to keep house for Anne Shirley, Stella, Priscilla, and Philippa Gordon at Patty's Place, bringing along her pet cat, the Sarah-cat. During her time keeping house at Patty's Place, she also adopted the cats Joseph and Rusty. Following the girls' graduation from Redmond College, she took the cats home with her and later set off to India to explore her daughter's mission field despite her intense fear of snakes.

_Sources: [v3 c9 P13](../source/v03-c09.md#nw-v03-c09-p0013), [v3 c16 P23](../source/v03-c16.md#nw-v03-c16-p0023), [v3 c16 P58](../source/v03-c16.md#nw-v03-c16-p0058), [v3 c38 P8](../source/v03-c38.md#nw-v03-c38-p0008), [v4 c3 P16](../source/v04-c03.md#nw-v04-c03-p0016)_

## Background by volume

- named after her father James who drowned at sea before her birth  <sub>[v3 c9 P13](../source/v03-c09.md#nw-v03-c09-p0013)</sub>
- mother and husband forbade her from having a yellow silk dress  <sub>[v3 c19 P6](../source/v03-c19.md#nw-v03-c19-p0006)</sub>
- prayed that her daughter Elizabeth would become a missionary  <sub>[v3 c36 P11](../source/v03-c36.md#nw-v03-c36-p0011)</sub>
- taught her daughter to cook before college  <sub>[v3 c27 P6](../source/v03-c27.md#nw-v03-c27-p0006)</sub>
- given a cat named Sarah-cat by her washerwoman  <sub>[v3 c16 P58](../source/v03-c16.md#nw-v03-c16-p0058)</sub>
- suggested a rubber band ear-training method to an old suitor  <sub>[v3 c37 P40](../source/v03-c37.md#nw-v03-c37-p0040)</sub>
- traveled to India despite her fear of snakes  <sub>[v4 c3 P16](../source/v04-c03.md#nw-v04-c03-p0016)</sub>

## Quotes

> I’m old enough to indulge myself in the matter of shoes and opinions. I mean to take it real easy here. I know you expect me to look after you and keep you proper, but I’m not going to do it. You’re old enough to know how to behave if you’re ever going to be. So, as far as I am concerned, you can all go to destruction in your own way.  <sub>[v3 c16 P53](../source/v03-c16.md#nw-v03-c16-p0053)</sub>

> Her name was Sarah, so my husband always called puss the Sarah-cat. She is eight years old, and a remarkable mouser. Don’t worry, Stella. The Sarah-cat never fights and Joseph rarely.  <sub>[v3 c16 P59](../source/v03-c16.md#nw-v03-c16-p0059)</sub>

> Mine’s cracked in a hundred places. Your Miss Stacy likely meant that when you are twenty your character would have got its permanent bent in one direction or ’tother, and would go on developing in that line. Don’t worry over it, Anne. Do your duty by God and your neighbor and yourself, and have a good time. That’s my philosophy and it’s always worked pretty well. Where’s Phil off to tonight?  <sub>[v3 c19 P4](../source/v03-c19.md#nw-v03-c19-p0004)</sub>

> The very first thing I’m going to do when I get to heaven is to get a yellow silk dress.  <sub>[v3 c19 P6](../source/v03-c19.md#nw-v03-c19-p0006)</sub>

> It isn’t in good taste to make fun of your beaux; but, I always did it myself.  <sub>[v3 c35 P21](../source/v03-c35.md#nw-v03-c35-p0021)</sub>
